headings.title: SMTO-CTX-0047 — This attached file needs its own reader, not plain text

html:
SMTO-CTX-0047 — This attached file needs its own reader, not plain text

GUID: 32da9d9b-28b7-53c8-a5e4-f151118874a0
Slug: attachment-reader-required
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: attachments

What happened

  • SMTO tried to read a PDF, Office document, image or archive as plain text. Those files need a special reader, so SMTO stopped rather than read them wrongly.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task is still running, let it continue. SMTO is told which reader the file needs and usually switches to it by itself. The error names the correct reader, so SMTO doesn't need you to re-attach anything.
  2. If SMTO asks for approval to use PDF documents, Office documents or Vision, approve it. Those are the skills that can open this kind of file properly.
  3. If that skill is turned off, ask the person who manages SMTO to allow it under Settings › Setup › Capabilities, then send your request again. Once the skill is allowed, it's safe to try again and SMTO can open the file.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the file with the right reader and its answer uses the file's contents.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name and type, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the file's contents as plain text unless you only need its words; tables, layout and pictures would be lost.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The shared text reader recognized a PDF, Office, image or archive attachment (by name, media type or byte signature) and refused to decode it as text; its format-specific reader must be used.

What this means

  • A document/image/archive filename, media type or byte signature was recognized by the shared text reader. Parsing has not been silently enabled. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • A document/image/archive filename, media type or byte signature was recognized by the shared text reader. Parsing has not been silently enabled.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • decode_text raised reader_required with the attachment descriptor's read_action (pdf.text, office.inspect, vision.analyze or file.inspect_archive) and required_skill. Use that read action; if the skill isn't loaded, enable it through discover_tools under normal approval, and make sure the PDF documents, Office documents, Vision or file skill is permitted in Settings > Setup > Capabilities.
  • Use the attachment’s returned read action. Discover and authorize its required skill through the normal task flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected authorized format reader returns content and source coverage.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
